Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR CORK AND CELLULOSE BASE JOINTING MATERIAL
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 January 1970, after the draft finalized by the Gaskets and Packings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 The cork and cellulose base jointing material covered by this standard is suitable for use at temperatures not exceeding 120�C in systems involving contact with mineral or di-ester type lubricating oil, mineral oil type It is not recommended for use with hydraulic fluid and petroleum fuel. water-based fluids. 0.3 The jointing material conforming to this standard deleterious attack by mould growth under tropical storage is suitable for commercial and defence purposes. is resistant to conditions and

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number.of significant places retained in the rounded off IS : 2-19602. value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of compressible sheet, jointing material composed of a mixture of cork granule and cellulosic fibres, from which gaskets can be cut or stamped. 2. GRADES 2.1 Cork and cellulose base jointing material grades, namely, Grade A and Grade B. shall be manufactured in two

MATERIALANDMANUFAGTURE 3.1 Grade A - The finished material shall consist of one or more plies of paper and cork composition impregnated with plasticized gelatine which is subsequently rendered insoluble with formaldehyde. The plasticizer shall be glycerine or a mixture of glycerine and sorbitol containing not more The glycerine shall be of technical grade quality than 50 percent sorbitol. complying with the requirements of IS : 1796-1961*. 3.2 Grade B - The composition discretion of the manufacturer. specified in 3.1 may be modified at the

3.3 The paper used in the manufacture of the jointing shall not contain During the manufacture a suitable fungicide shall mechanical wood pulp. be incorporated to render the finished material resistant to mould growth. The composition of the fungicide shall be as agreed to between manufacturer and purchaser. 3.4 The material of both Grade A and Grade B types shall being cut or punched without cracking, tearing or separation 3.5 The jointing 1 060 mm wide. 4. 7.1.5.1 The conductivity of the water extract of material prepared as described in Appendix D shall be not greater than 175 micromhos/cm when determined as described in 7.4 of IS : 4420-1967'.

7.1.5.2 For material which does not comply with the requirements of 7.1.5.1, the chloride content of the material shall not exceed 0.17 percent when determined as sodium chloride ( NaCl) and the sulphate content shall not exceed 0.15 percent when determined as anhydrous sodium sulphate ( NasSO, ) when determined as described in D-3 of Appendix D. 7.1.5.3 The PH value of the water extract of the material, determined as described in D-2 of Appendix D, shall be not less than 6 or greater than 8.5. tested as described in Appendix E, 7.1.6 Dimensional Stability -When the change in length of the test specimen shall not exceed 1.5 percent in any direction. 7.2 Type Tests - These .shall include (a) flexibility, and (b) resistance to mould growth, and shall be carried out at such reduced frequency as may be agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 7.2.1 Flexibilily - The flexibility of the material shall be such that when tested by the method described in Appendix F the test pieces shall not crack or separate into layers. 7.2.2 Resistance to Mould Growth (forGrade A Jointing only ) - When the material is tested as described in Appendix G, there shall be no visible mould growth on any part of the test pieces.

A-2.1 The rolls of jointing selected according to A-l.2 shall be examined If the number of rolls found not in conformity with the for dimensions. specified requirements is less than or equal to the corresponding number given in co1 3 of Table 1, the lot shall be declared conforming to the requirements for dimensions. B-l.2 The compressibility

of the material shall two dial indicators graduated in millimetres and shall be rigidly attached to the upper loading the diameter, with their spindles resting on the datum level.

B-2. TEST SPECIMENS B-2.1 The specimens circular in shape and of area 5 cm2 shall be punched For samples of thickness I.60 mm and from the sample with a sharp die. 20 such specimens shall be cut. For sample thicknesses above, between 0.80 and 1.60 mm, 40 such specimens shall be cut and from these a composite specimen for testing shall be prepared by pairing together two specimens selected at random without the use of adhesive.
B-2.2 Materials of thickness less than 0.80 mm cannot be tested the practical difficulty in making satisfactory measurement. B-3. CONDITIONING owing to

B-3.1 The specimens

shall be dried over silica gel for not less than 18 hours and then exposed to an atmosphere of 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27 + 2�C. Five of the specimens shall be weighed to an accuracy of O*OOl g Immediately and at 24-hour intervals thereafter. The specimens must show a gain in weight after the first 24 hour period and when they show neither gain nor loss in weight exceeding 1*O percent in each of two consecutive 24 hour periods, all the specimens may be considered to have reached equilibrium and testin g may begin. Where it is not possible to carry out the compression testing in a conditioned room: the samples shall 9

IS : 5569 - 1970 be removed from the conditioning atmosphere one at a time and transported to the test apparatus in a sealed container and tested immediately.
NOTE - The conditioning of specimens shal1 procedure laid down, as it is known that departure ally affect the subsequent results. be strictly in accordance with the from this in any way may materi-

B-4. METHOD

FOR DETERMINATION

OF JIG YIELD

B-4.1 The jig yield is defined as the deflection of the apparatus caused by the increase from the pre-load to the major load. This jig yield shall be determined immediately prior to each series of tests by adopting the following procedure without the insertion of test specimens: a) Apply pre-load of 35 kgf and maintain this for two minutes before recording the mean dial gauge readings (Jo). Increase the load at a steady rate to the major load of 450 kgf and maintain this for two minutes before recording the mean dial gauge readings (JJ. Reduce the load to the pre-load of 35 kgf and maintain this for 30 seconds before recording the mean dial gauge readings (34. The jig yield 3 = J1 - Jo.
NOTE- If the values of JO and J2 differ by more than 5 pm the apparatus is showing non-elastic yield and is not in a suitable condition for carrying out the tests.

b) A sufficient number of such determinations shall be made until the maximum and minimum of five consecutive determinations do not differ by more than 7 Pm. The mean of these five values shall constitute jig yield of the apparatus. B-5. METHOD OF TEST

B-5.1 The pre-load of 35 kgf shall be applied with no test specimen in place and the mean of two dial gauge readings (&) shall be recorded. The procedure shall be repeated with the specimens placed centrally between the platens and this load maintained constant for two minutes. The mean of the two dial gauge readings (T1) shall be recorded. The load shall then be increased at a steady rate over a period of 20 to 30 seconds to fqr two minutes the major load of 450 kgf. This load shall be maintained when the mean of the two dial gauge readings (TJ shall again be recorded. The total load shall then be removed and the sample allowed to recover for two minutes in the free state. The pre-load of 35 kgf shall then be reapplied and after 30 seconds under this load the mean of the two dial gauge readings (7-s) shall again be recorded. Twenty determinations shall be carried out on each batch of material. 10

D

(Clauses 7.1.5.1, 7.1.5.2 and 7.1.5.3)
METHOD OF TEST CORROSIvE OF WATER FOR FREEDOM IMPURITIES EXTRACT FROM

D-l.

PREPARATION

D-l.1 Apparatus - The extraction apparatus shall consist of a 500-ml borosilicate glass'flask to which is attached by means of a ground glass 12

Is : 5!569- 1970 joint an efficient reflux condenser, fitted with a guard tube with a suitable reagent for the exclusion of carbon dioxide and atmospheric impurities. D-1.2 Procedure D-1.2.1 Cut out a portion of the sample of material into pieces about 6 mmf weigh about 10 g into the flask and add to this test portion 20 times Fit the reflux condenser and guard its weight of demineralized water. tube, heat the water to boiling point and continue boiling gently for one' hour. Replace the reflux condenser by a stoppeand guard tube and cool to room temperature. D-1.2.2 Immediately before preparing the water extract, boil about 100 ml of the demineralized water in the apparatus for one hour. Stopper the flask and cool. The apparatus shall be considered to be satisfactory of the water is not greater than if the electrical conductivity 2 micromhos/cm.
NOTE--~ order to comply with the above requirement, it will normally be necessary to use demineralized water, having an electrical conductivity not greater than 1 micromho/cm.

D-2. DETERMINATION

OF pH VALUE OF WATER EXTRACT

D-2.1 A portion of the water extract of the material shall be decanted into a suitable cell and the @-I value determined in accordance with 10 of The determination shall be made as soon as IS : 1060 ( Part I )-1966*. the water extract has cooled to room temperature. The cell shall be rinsed with the demineralized water immediately before using. D-3. DETERMINATION CONTENTS OF CHLORIDE AND SULPHATE

D-3.1 A suitable aliquot portion equivalent to W grams of sample of the extract prepared according to D-l shall be taken and evaporated to nearly 10 ml, Approximately 0.05 g of analytical reagent grade sodium hydroxide shall be added and allowed to dissolve. The solution shall be transferred quantitatively to a platinum crucible and evaporated to dryness. The crucible shall be heated in a muffle furnace for four hours at 700 + lo%, removed, allowed to cool, and placed in a beaker. The residue shall be dissolved in 25 ml of 5 percent ( weight/volume ) nitric acid, by warming

APPENDIX ( CZause 7.2.2 )
METHOD G-l. TEST PIECES

G

FOR DETERMINATION OF RESISTANCE TO MOULD GROWTH

G-l.1 The test pieces used shall be strips approximately 12 mm wide. G-2. PREPARATION OF AQUEOUS SPORE

100 mm long and

SUSPENSION

G-2.1 The mixed aqueous spore suspension shall be freshly prepared by transferring a small mass of spores from each of the seven cultures listed in G-2.2 to about 20 millilitres of distilled water conforming to IS : 10701960" in a spray bottle. The contents of the spray bottle shall be thoroughly shaken before use. G-2.2 The cultures used for preparation the following: Aspergillus uiger Aspergillus amstelodami PaecilomyGes varioti Stachybotrys atra Chaeton+um globosum Penicillium breoi-compactum Penicillium &opium
*Specification for water, distilled quality ( rcti~ed ).

of the mixed spore suspension are

17

IS:5569-1970 G-3. PROCEDURE G-3.1 Each test piece shall be inoculated with a fine spray of the mixed aqueous spore suspension described in G-2, care being taken not to saturate the material with water. Each test piece shall then be placed longitudinally in a test tube so that it is supported by the tube. The tube shall be placed upright over water in a closed glass container, such as a vacuum desiccator, fitted with a short capillary tube to retain the substantially stagnant atmosphere saturated with moisture but to allow slight breathing. G-3.2 This container shall then be placed for 28 days in humidity control chambers capable of maintaining a temperature of 30 f 2�C and relative humidity between 90 and 98 percent. G-3.3 The test piece shall then be removed examined for mould growth. from the container and
